clue.text: Robin, batting three sessions, on strike regularly

parts.note: Sir Robin Day was a famous British television interviewer
a batsman batting is said to be in
a day's play in Test cricket is split into three sessions
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A cricketer called Robin, batting through three sessions, faces the bowling turn after turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture hides a name: Robin Day was a British political broadcaster. 'On strike' is cricket talk in the surface but means industrial action in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something happening every single day without a break, hence routinely.

clue.text: Eager to lay off Department with a number of birds

indicators.note: to lay off is to dismiss, so the department's letter is sacked from the word

parts.note: avid means keen or eager

explanation.surface: A keen boss is told to sack a department along with a number of its birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to birds, as in avian flu.

clue.text: Rock musician quietly leaves unpaid, having mixed tracks

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaves means goes away from the word, so the quiet letter is dropped from it

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
RY, railway, gives the tracks a train runs on

explanation.surface: A rock musician slips away without paying, after remixing some tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quietly leaves' takes P from UNPAID to leave UNAID; 'mixed' rearranges that as IANDU. Ian Dury was the singer of the Blockheads.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Dury was a British singer, frontman of the Blockheads, famous in punk and new wave rock.

clue.text: Faulty line somewhere in the Midlands

parts.note: a dud is a faulty thing that fails to work
a ley is a line, as in a ley line linking ancient sites

explanation.surface: A faulty railway line is reported somewhere in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Midlands is the central region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a town in the West Midlands of England, an example of a place in that region.

clue.text: Love reading over newspaper in the old park

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the archaic word

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: in this down clue, reading over means the paper's name runs upwards, backwards

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone fond of reading a newspaper in an old park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' as O comes from tennis, where love is nil; 'reading over' works upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous national park in California, an example of a park.

clue.text: Head from crossroads for some oil?

indicators.note: head from means the first letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: a crossroads is a road junction

explanation.surface: Someone heads away from a crossroads to fetch some oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head from' removes J, the head of JUNCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Anointing with oil, or the oil or ointment itself, is this ritual word, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Director type jogging on lap with runner

parts.note: roman is a style of typeface

indicators.note: jogging means jolting about, so these letters are shaken up

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow

explanation.surface: A film director type goes jogging round a lap with a runner beside him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogging' rearranges ON LAP as POLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman Polanski is a Polish-French film director, maker of Chinatown and Rosemary's Baby.

clue.text: Boxer hurt unknown, punching so long

parts.note: to mar is to hurt or damage

indicators.note: punching means the unknown letter is driven into the farewell

parts.note: ciao is an Italian goodbye, so long
N is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A boxer is hurt by an unknown opponent, after punching for so long.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky Marciano was the unbeaten American heavyweight boxing champion of the 1950s.

clue.text: Film pioneer agrees montage looks unusual

indicators.note: looks unusual says the letters of the words look odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: A film pioneer agrees that the montage looks odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks unusual' rearranges AGREES MONTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eastman founded Kodak and introduced roll film, a pioneer of photography and cinema.

clue.text: Working couple nett minimum of income — it could bring tears to your eyes

definitions.text: it could bring tears to your eyes

indicators.note: to nett is to catch, so the pair of words captures the letter
couple means two of them, so the word appears twice

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

indicators.note: minimum of means just the smallest part, the first letter of income

explanation.surface: A working couple whose nett income is minimal, enough to bring tears to anyone's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' doubles ON to ONON; 'nett' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this vegetable releases a compound that irritates the eyes and makes them water.

clue.text: Dry river banks animal's tracking thus

indicators.note: banks means lines either side, so the river encloses the rest

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so the animal comes after

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal tracks along the dry banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' is a verb: DEE holds SIC followed by CAT ('tracking').
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to remove the moisture from something completely.

clue.text: Amanda creepily retained employment to a disgusting extent

indicators.note: retained means held within, so the jumbled name holds the rest
creepily suggests the name moves strangely, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: employment is use

explanation.surface: Amanda kept her job in a creepy way, which disgusted everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The name looks like the subject of the sentence, but its letters are the fodder; the jumbled ADNAAM is split by the employment word.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning to the point of sickness, hence repeated until revolting.

clue.text: Such entertainment, endlessly racing around

indicators.note: around signals the remaining letters are moved about
endlessly means without its final letter

explanation.surface: This kind of entertainment comes with endless racing around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts G from RACING; 'around' rearranges RACIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio and music played while driving is called in-car entertainment, so the term qualifies this kind of amusement.

clue.text: Sailor having nip by optic

parts.note: to nip somewhere is to pop there quickly
an optic is an eye

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a nip of spirits from a bar optic.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is a British pub measure dispenser on a spirit bottle, but here means an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye is the spinach-eating cartoon sailor man.

clue.text: Couple in Perth start to buy jewellery — superficial decoration at seaside?

indicators.note: couple in means keep just a pair of letters from the start of the city, losing the rest
start to means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A couple in Perth start to buy some jewellery for the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple in Perth' keeps only its first two letters, dropping RTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering a surface with small stones is a beach-like finish, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Wise entertained adversely, not close to Morecambe for a long period

indicators.note: entertained means hosted, so the wise word holds the rest

parts.note: sage means wise

indicators.note: adversely means unfavourably, read as an instruction to upset the letters
close to means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Ernie Wise entertained badly without Eric Morecambe for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British comedy double act. 'Adversely' rearranges NOT plus E as TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric era of stone tools lasted for millions of years, a long period.

clue.text: Glorify rebellious nobleman alienating leader around Zimbabwe's capital

indicators.note: around means the jumble encircles the capital letter
rebellious suggests a revolt, so the letters turn over into a new order
alienating leader means pushing away the word's first letter
capital means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rebellious nobleman alienates his leader around Harare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alienating leader' drops N from NOBLEMAN; 'rebellious' rearranges OBLEMAN as EMBLAON, which goes 'around' Z.
explanation.definitionFit: To emblazon is to celebrate or extol conspicuously, a synonym of praising lavishly.

clue.text: By box office, man wears flamboyant fabric for opera

indicators.note: wears means is inside, so the fabric goes around the pieces

parts.note: lamé is a showy fabric woven with metallic thread
he is a man

explanation.surface: Near the box office, a man wears flamboyant fabric for the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera about bohemians in Paris.

clue.text: Work with needles when a placing outside leads to Drug Squad

indicators.note: outside means the arranged letters go around the others
placing means arranging, so these letters are put in a new order
leads to means the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: Police arrange themselves outside, with leads to the Drug Squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Placing' rearranges WHEN A as HANEW, which goes 'outside' DS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stitch by hand with a needle and thread, so a verb for needlework.

clue.text: Ball kept in play wonderfully by a backhander

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the shuffled word contains the round letter
wonderfully suggests an amazing twist, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a ball is round, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tennis player keeps the ball in play wonderfully with a backhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonderfully' rearranges PLAY as PAYL, which holds O.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe, especially one paid for radio airplay, is a backhander.

clue.text: Best writing, perhaps, with Biro that's sharp

parts.note: ace means excellent, the best
writing is one of the three Rs, so R
a Bic is a ballpoint pen, like a Biro

explanation.surface: The best writing perhaps comes with a Biro that's sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so R can stand for writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic remarks are sharp and biting in tone.

clue.text: Plain fish contains bones

indicators.note: contains means the fish holds the other piece inside

parts.note: tuna is a fish
bones, short for sawbones, is slang for a doctor, DR

explanation.surface: A plain fish full of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain.

clue.text: Centre of banner contains odd bits of yellow material

indicators.note: contains means those middle letters hold the other piece
centre of means the middle letters of the word
odd bits of means the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: The middle of a banner has odd bits of yellow material.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of BANNER is NN, holding YLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fabric or fibre, an example of a material.

clue.text: Round American splits garden tool turning over plant

indicators.note: splits means breaks open the reversed tool to sit inside it
turning over means the tool's name is read backwards

parts.note: a trowel is a garden tool
something round is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A round American splits his garden tool turning over a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning over' gives LEWORT, which OUS 'splits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lousewort is a wild flower, a semi-parasitic plant of damp heaths.

clue.text: Two rejected buffalo cuts?

indicators.note: rejected means two letters are thrown out and the rest tossed into a new order

parts.note: two stands for a pair of letters thrown out, here the opening pair of the animal's name

explanation.surface: Two buffalo cuts are sent back as unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two rejected' takes two letters, B and U, out of BUFFALO; 'rejected' also signals the remaining FFALO being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the organ meat butchers sell, so the question mark marks it as types of cut.

clue.text: Having the stature of a man involved in mating — on this bed?

definitions.text: Having the stature of a man involved in mating — on this bed?

parts.words: Having the stature of a man involved in mating — on this bed?
parts.note: the chess piece checkmated is the monarch, so having his stature describes a large bed

explanation.surface: A man's size measured by his love life, on this bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mating' looks romantic, but in chess the piece that is mated is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest standard bed size is named after royalty, matching the chess monarch.

clue.text: Book later verbally proposed for award

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the words sound like the answer

parts.note: B is a standard abbreviation for book; after means later

explanation.surface: Someone books a later slot verbally, then is proposed for an award.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Academy of Film and Television Arts gives prizes, a film award.

clue.text: Folk singer gets on well with Macca when touring

indicators.note: when touring suggests going round, so these letters travel into new places

explanation.surface: A folk singer gets on well with Paul McCartney on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Macca is a nickname for Paul McCartney. 'When touring' rearranges ON WELL MACCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewan MacColl was a British folk musician who wrote The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face.
